definitions: An options strategy involving selling an out-of-the-money put option and buying a further out-of-the-money put option with the same expiration date, used when an investor expects a moderate increase in the underlying asset's price.
A credit spread strategy where the investor profits if the underlying asset's price stays above the strike price of the sold put option.
examples: The trader initiated a bull put spread.
His bull put spread expired worthless.
A bull put spread limits both profit and loss.
